chapter: Kansas City rooms and Piney Brown
title: Thamon Hayes becomes Harlan Leonard's Rockets, and the 1936 breakup
summary: Goodwin explains Hayes's union trouble, Leonard fronting the band, the failed Chicago trips and how members split into small groups.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Of course. We jammed a lot when Baby and I were playing together in a big band; Thoman Hayes' band and also the band that changed to be the Kansas City Rockets, Harlan headed by Leonard. We would go down there and we'd still go there and jam; the same consequences.
You and Baby left Thoman Hayes to go with Harlan Leonard's Rockets, Harlan Leonard's band?

Well, the band was originally Thoman's band. Thoman had a little union trouble and Harlan was voted to front the band and from then on, well Harlan did have the band. After trips to Chicago and around and down in the southern part of the country, at this time Harlan was the head of the band.

You know RCA about three years ago reissued on an LP the great Harlan Leonard band. Ernie Williams, for example, did about three vocals. Let's see, who was on that band? I know the Walter Brothers were, weren't

None of the originals that were with him before. See, possibly getting a little ahead of my story, Harlan Leonard's band also -- the Kansas City Rockets also broke up in 1936, after our second unsuccessful trip to Chicago to try to make it big and I guess most of the guys figured, "Well, this is enough. We want to play music but we will also dedicate ourselves to making a living and getting the best out of it", and then we all branched off into smaller groups.

I started playing with Buster Smith at a place called Lucille's Paradise and Baby Lovett, Herman Walder, Jack Johnson, a little place there and Pete Johnson, the great Pete Walder Johnson, the boogie woogie piano player, and the brothers, Herman and Woodie, and I believe there were six members in that band, I think I named all six of them. Well they went to play at 12th and Truce at a place called the Spinning Wheel, and this was part of the band that was a part of Leonard's band; that is, the Kansas City Rockets, and then there was another part of the band -- it's a little vague to me now, let me see, I'm trying to think of who was left, right now it escapes me -- but this is part of the way the band went in separate ways.

Well, we'll come back to the Spinning Wheel when we get into the rooms that were in town that we're going to cover. That's very interesting, Crook's description of what happened to the Harlem Leonard great band. We'll be right back ladies and gentlemen.
